evidence.source: CUHK 漢語多功能字庫, 漢字甲骨部件分析
evidence.text: The entry describes the oracle-bone form as 舁 plus 同: four hands jointly lifting a tube- or bucket-like object; the center may also have a 口 below. It gives the basic sense as “rise/get up.” It reports oracle-bone uses as a personal or state name, cites a reading of 同 as 興 in a divinatory text about an illness improving, and records bronze-inscription uses as a personal or clan name and in the sense “mobilize/raise troops.” It also cites bamboo and silk manuscript uses for “arise,” “raise troops,” and “levy labor,” as well as received-text examples.
evidence.title: 漢字甲骨部件分析：興

evidence.field: 說文釋形、字樣說明、釋義與引例
evidence.text: The dictionary records the received Shuowen explanation 起也。从舁，从同。同力也 and the reading 虛陵切. Its entry separates xīng and xìng readings and lists meanings and examples including rising or occurring, getting up, raising troops, founding, flourishing, poetic 興, interest and pleasure. These are dictionary-recorded attestations, not a dated sequence of semantic change. The entry does not provide publicly viewable oracle-bone or bronze plates in this page.
evidence.title: [A03399] 興 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Shuowen.org, received 說文解字 and 段玉裁注
evidence.text: The entry gives “起也。从舁从同。同力也.” Duan Yucai labels the analysis 會意 and comments that the graph explains 同力. It also quotes Guangyun senses 盛、舉、善 and notes the Zhouli poetic category 興. This supports the received lexicographic account but is not independent proof of the graph’s original design.
evidence.title: 說文解字「興」

evidence.source: 教育部國語辭典 / CUHK 漢語多功能字庫 cited texts
evidence.text: The sources cite 詩經〈衛風·氓〉“夙興夜寐” and 論語〈衛靈公〉“從者病，莫能興” for getting up; 呂氏春秋 and 史記 for arising or a polity’s rise; 詩經〈秦風·無衣〉 and bronze tiger tally text for mobilizing troops; and later examples for flourishing and 兴致. CUHK also gives named manuscript contexts: Guodian 唐虞之道, Mawangdui 戰國縱橫家書, and Shuihudi 秦律十八種. The entry does not provide artifact-specific dating for each cited manuscript passage; precise chronological ordering of senses is therefore not established here.
evidence.kind: cited textual evidence as reported by reference
evidence.title: 漢字甲骨部件分析：興

evidence.text: The page presents oracle-bone, bronze, small-seal, and standard forms and explains the ancient forms as 舁 and 同, resembling four hands lifting a mold. It says the standard form resembles small seal. The image links were not visually inspected, so this is recorded as the page’s textual assertion rather than an independently verified image sequence.
evidence.title: 字源考釋 - 興

evidence.text: The official character page gives 興, kMandarin xìng, and identifies U+5174 兴 as its kSimplifiedVariant. Local supplied rows additionally show kMandarin xìng for both 興 and 兴 in sources/unihan/Unihan_Readings.txt; these are local dataset rows, not external web pages. The displayed Unihan page was inspected at the codepoint URL requested for U+8208; it verifies the traditional character’s record and its relation to the simplified codepoint.
evidence.title: Unihan data for U+8208

evidence.field: Old Chinese readings and conflicting graph account
evidence.text: The page’s glyph-origin section calls 興 an ideogrammic compound showing four hands lifting an object, and says the central object varies in oracle-bone and early bronze forms before becoming standardized as 同. Its reading section lists Zhengzhang Old Chinese *qʰɯŋ and *qʰɯŋs and Baxter–Sagart *qʰ(r)əŋ for 興. The local Baxter–Sagart table supplied in the prompt independently gives 興 MC xing and OC *qʰ(r)əŋ, gloss “lift, rise” (sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv, row 興). This differs from dossier’s imported *qʰɯŋ transcription where it is attributed to Baxter–Sagart; the two notations belong to distinct reconstruction systems and must not be merged. The imported claim that 型 (*ɡeːŋ) is the phonetic element is not supported by the primary references inspected; CUHK and Shuowen/ Duan instead analyze 舁 and 同 semantically/associatively. No independently verified evidence here establishes 型 as a sound component.
evidence.kind: secondary reading comparison and disputed analysis
evidence.title: 興 - Wiktionary, the free dictionary

evidence.text: U+8208’s official page gives kMandarin xìng, kDefinition “thrive, prosper, flourish,” and kSimplifiedVariant U+5174 兴. For the simplified character, the official linked record is https://www.unicode.org/cgi-bin/GetUnihanData.pl?codepoint=5174; opening that direct URL failed in the web tool, but the record is linked from the inspected 興 page. Local supplied kMandarin rows report xìng for both forms. Current Unihan readings establish modern metadata only, not ancient sound relationships.
evidence.kind: official metadata with access limitation for related record
evidence.title: Unihan data for U+8208

search_audit.outcome: Searched for primary dictionary and paleographic evidence; inspected the MOE dictionary and Shuowen entry. The MOE page supports the received Shuowen form and records classical citations.

search_audit.outcome: Found and inspected CUHK and ePhonetics character-specific analyses. Their text supports a four-hand lifting interpretation; no inspected source supported the alleged 型 phonetic.

search_audit.outcome: Search surfaced general character-history material and dated-text dictionaries, but CUHK’s specific page supplied the useful graph and usage evidence.

search_audit.outcome: Inspected CUHK’s textual examples and the Wiktionary collation. CUHK gives separate classical, bronze, and manuscript contexts; chronology among senses is not inferred from the gloss list.

search_audit.query: Simplified Characters in Traditional Text simplified form 興 cursive
search_audit.outcome: Inspected simplified-character entry, which labels 兴 as simplified 興 and a cursive abbreviation (ryakuji in its Japanese section). The official Unihan record also identifies 兴 as the simplified variant. The exact historical cursive derivation was not verified in a primary paleographic source.

gaps: The inspected sources consistently support a semantic/ideogrammic analysis involving 舁 and 同/central object, but no directly inspected primary oracle-bone facsimile was independently read. Descriptions of the center as a lifting tray, tube, bucket, or mold are source interpretations; the exact depicted object and its original name are not established here.

The Shuowen account dates to the received lexicographic tradition, not the graph’s creation. The accessible evidence reports oracle-bone examples and later bronze/manuscript examples but does not give artifact-level dating for every cited item, so it cannot establish a complete chronology of graphic forms or semantic changes.

The dossier’s 型 phonetic analysis conflicts with the inspected primary-style graph explanations. No evidence located in the bounded searches establishes 型 as a component or supports that proposed phonetic role; the exact source of this claim may be a transcription or analysis error.

A named phonetic component was not established for 興 by the inspected sources. Baxter–Sagart *qʰ(r)əŋ and Zhengzhang *qʰɯŋ are separate reconstructions of 興, not evidence that 型 is its phonetic element.

The traditional character’s official Unihan page was verified. The direct U+5174 official page failed to open, so the simplified character’s exact external kMandarin row could not be inspected independently; the supplied local row reports xìng for 兴. Local source path is not an external citation.

The local supplied Baxter–Sagart record contains only 興, not a separate row for any proposed sound component. Since 型 is not supported as the component, no component/host historical sound comparison is warranted. Local readings are metadata checks, not evidence of ancient sound relations.

The potential Burmese comparison in the dossier remains unverified and speculative; no evidence in the inspected sources demonstrates a borrowing relationship. No whole-graph phonetic-loan claim was needed for the supported analysis.
No judgment about reuse rights or a repeatable local extract is made. The research uses concise page-specific paraphrases; permission for bulk reuse was not established.
